questions.question: Attachments you send in the chat: today reading one costs up to 3 taps, and the spec as written keeps 'attachment reads' in its fail-closed list. Should a file the requester sent in this conversation be readable with zero taps (birthright), while attachments from anyone else stay judged?
Scheduled jobs: the spec promises 'a scheduled job stops re-asking every run' (AC3) but decision 0121 says the autonomous lane never consults the learned-decision memory. Which way?
options: Drop the job promise from AC3 (Recommended)
Jobs consult learned decisions as grants
questions.chosen: Jobs consult learned decisions as grants

questions.question: What does a tap mean? The spec currently learns BOTH 'Allow once' and 'Allow for future'. Fable's UX read: once must never be remembered; the remembered choice should be the default button.

Folder scope: your 10-taps-in-3-minutes run was all reads under ~/Workdir. Should an Allow offer 'this folder from now on', learned as a trusted root, so later reads there are deterministic yes (no judge, no tap) — also removing the read storm if the judge is ever down?
